title: Luminal - Search-Based Deep Learning Compilers - Joe Fioti
talk_summary: Joe Fioti presents Luminal, a deep-learning inference compiler that represents models as graphs of ~12 primitive ops and recovers performance by searching over logically-equivalent GPU kernels via egglog rewrite rules, then applying deterministic passes (buffer reuse, batched kernel launch).

takeaways.technique: Search over equivalent implementations instead of hand-written rules
takeaways.what_they_do: They encode a small set of correctness-preserving rewrite rules, expand a large space of logically equivalent kernels, then profile candidates and keep the fastest; Monte Carlo search prunes when exhaustive profiling is infeasible.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can write a whole bunch of simple rules to build this big search space and then let the search go through and find the fastest kernels
takeaways.numbers: ~20-25 rewrite rules; found flash attention automatically

takeaways.technique: Batch dispatch to cut round-trip overhead
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of CPU dispatching one GPU kernel and waiting, they queue all kernels ahead of time so the accelerator runs them back-to-back, removing per-step launch latency.
takeaways.evidence_quote: what if we were to dispatch all of our kernels ahead of time uh and then the GPU would just run through them one by one
